en.greeting: Hi! Today you go beyond the words: decode the polite code people use at work, say things indirectly yourself when it fits, catch irony and understatement, and hear what an answer means by what it avoids. Play each recording as often as you like.

steps.title: The polite code
steps.text: At C1 you heard understatement, irony, reluctance, the polite no and faint praise in the words. Now go further: the polite code people use at work, especially British speakers.
steps.body: These soft phrases carry a stronger message. The big one: **I'm not sure that's the best idea** usually means **I disagree**, not real doubt. How to tell: real doubt **asks for information** (*I'm not sure: when does testing finish?*); the code is followed by a **reason against** or an **alternative** (*Perhaps we could…*). These are tendencies, not rules: context decides.

pairs.en: I'm not sure that's the best idea.
pairs.id: Aku kurang yakin itu ide terbaik. → aku tidak setuju
Dengan segala hormat, … → akan ada bantahan
Aku paham maksudmu. → tapi aku tidak setuju

pairs.en: It might be worth looking at…
pairs.id: Mungkin ada baiknya melihat… → sebaiknya diperiksa, ada masalah
Mungkin perlu dicek ulang… → menurutku ini salah
Berani juga. → berisiko, mungkin ceroboh
Akan saya ingat. → mungkin tidak ditindaklanjuti
Mungkin kita bisa mempertimbangkan… → aku ingin ini

steps.title: Listen: a reply to the director
steps.text: A marketing meeting in Jakarta. Listen for the code phrases, then look at what follows them.

question.listen: Spending the whole budget on one TV advert? I hear what you're saying, Pak Rudi, and it's certainly a brave plan. It might be worth looking at what happened with last year's campaign first. And perhaps keeping some money back for online ads.
options: She has no opinion yet and wants to hear more about the plan.
She thinks the plan is too risky and wants a smaller, safer one.
She admires the plan and wants to start soon.
question.prompt: In a marketing meeting, the director, Pak Rudi, suggests spending the whole year's budget on one TV advert. Listen to Sari's reply. What does she really mean?
question.explanation: **I hear what you're saying** (= but I don't agree) and **a brave plan** (= risky) are polite code. Then come an alternative to check first (**It might be worth looking at** last year's campaign) and a safer plan (**keeping some money back** for online ads). She has a clear opinion: she asks no question about the plan, she argues for a smaller one.

steps.title: Saying it indirectly yourself
steps.text: Now the other side: using the code yourself, and knowing when not to.
steps.body: Be indirect when the relationship matters: declining, criticising a senior person's idea, hinting. Be direct about safety, money and deadlines. Polite disagreement = **soften + reason + alternative**. British English is more understated (*not bad* = good; *quite good* often = only OK); American English is more direct. Indonesian bridge: *iya* often = I hear you, *nanti dulu* = a soft no, *boleh juga* = a careful yes. **Trap:** in English a polite *Yes* sounds like agreement.

pairs.en: I'm not sure that's the best idea: … Could we …?
pairs.id: lunakkan + alasan + alternatif → tidak setuju dengan sopan

pairs.en: That's very kind of you, but I'm afraid…
pairs.id: Baik sekali, tapi sayangnya… → menolak undangan
Sudah cukup malam. → kode: ayo selesai

pairs.en: Is it just me, or is it cold in here?
pairs.id: Cuma aku atau memang dingin di sini? → kode: AC-nya dikecilkan
Bagus! (British: pujian sungguhan)
Lumayan. (British: sering hanya 'oke')
Aku paham. → hanya 'aku dengar', bukan 'aku setuju'

steps.title: Your turn: disagree politely
steps.text: Choose the reply that is polite AND makes your disagreement clear.

options: Yes, of course, Bu Ani.
That's a terrible idea, Bu Ani. It won't work.
I'm not sure that's the best idea, Bu Ani: testing won't finish until the 20th. Could we keep the original date?
question.prompt: Your manager, Bu Ani, wants to move the product launch two weeks earlier. You think it's a bad idea because testing isn't finished. In a meeting with her and the team, which reply disagrees clearly but politely?
question.explanation: Soften (**I'm not sure that's the best idea**) + reason (testing won't finish until the 20th) + alternative (keep the original date). **Yes, of course** is polite, but she will hear agreement: the *iya* trap. **That's a terrible idea** is clear, but far too blunt for your manager in front of the team.

steps.title: Irony and understatement: the verbal cues
steps.text: British irony is often said in a flat voice, and our audio is one calm voice too. So the words are your evidence.
steps.body: **Irony:** positive words + a clearly bad situation, set phrases (*Oh great*, *Well, that went well*) or over-the-top praise = the opposite. **Sarcasm** is irony that mocks someone: careful. **Understatement:** much less than the truth (*not exactly cheap* = very expensive). **Litotes:** *not* + the opposite word (*not bad* = good, *hardly ideal* = bad). **Dry humour:** *I've had worse days* after a disaster = I'm coping. Compare the words with the facts; believe the facts.

pairs.id: Cuaca yang pas buat piknik. → (saat badai) cuacanya buruk sekali
Yah, lancar sekali. → (setelah bencana) gagal
Makasih banyak. → (ke orang yang bikin masalah) kesal
Tidak murah juga sih. → mahal sekali
tidak jelek → cukup menarik (pujian hati-hati)
bukan yang paling ramah → kurang ramah
jauh dari ideal → buruk
Yah, pernah lebih buruk. → (setelah bencana) humor kering: tetap tegar

steps.title: Listen: stuck at the airport
steps.text: Dimas phones a friend from the airport in Surabaya. Compare his words with the facts he gives.

question.listen: Well, this is fun. The flight's been delayed three times, the only café is closed, and my phone's on two per cent. Honestly, I couldn't have planned a better start to my holiday.
options: He's enjoying it.
He's annoyed, and he's joking about it.
He's worried about missing work.
question.prompt: Listen to Dimas. How does he really feel about the start of his holiday?
question.explanation: Irony: **this is fun** and **I couldn't have planned a better start** sit next to three bad facts (three delays, a closed café, a dying phone). The facts win: he's annoyed and making a joke of it. Nothing in his words is about work.

steps.title: Your turn: litotes
steps.text: Two pieces of understatement in one sentence. What's the real story?

options: The panel were rather unfriendly, and her answer about salary went badly.
The panel were very friendly, and her answer about salary was perfect.
The panel were friendly, but her answer about salary was a little short.
question.prompt: After a job interview in Jakarta, Rina's friend asks how it went. Rina says: 'The panel weren't the friendliest people I've ever met, and my answer about salary was hardly ideal.' What does she mean?
question.explanation: Litotes: **weren't the friendliest** = rather unfriendly, and **hardly ideal** = bad. Both soften a negative message. The second option takes the words in the opposite direction; the third invents a detail (a short answer) and misses that *hardly ideal* means it went badly.

steps.title: Subtext: what the answer avoids
steps.text: Last skill: hearing the message in what an answer leaves out.
steps.body: The philosopher Paul Grice described **the idea that** people in a conversation cooperate: they give enough information, say what's true, stay on topic and are clear. When an answer obviously doesn't, there's a message. Watch for: **avoiding the point**, **changing the topic**, **a reason instead of an answer**, **a weaker word** (*most*, *some*) and **no yes to a yes/no question**. If the answer were a simple yes, saying yes would be easy.

pairs.en: Did you like my presentation? — The slides were very colourful.
pairs.id: menghindari pokoknya → tidak terlalu suka

pairs.en: Is the project on schedule? — Have you tried the new coffee machine?
pairs.id: ganti topik → tidak, dan tidak mau membahasnya

pairs.en: Are you coming? — I've got an early flight tomorrow.
pairs.id: alasan, bukan jawaban → mungkin tidak

pairs.en: Did everyone sign? — Most of them did.
pairs.id: kata yang lebih lemah → belum semua

pairs.en: Will the office stay open? — We're reviewing all our options.
pairs.id: tidak ada 'ya' → tidak ada janji

steps.title: Listen: a question about profit
steps.text: A networking event in Jakarta. An investor asks Pak Hasan a direct question.

question.listen: A profit? Well, we've got a fantastic team, our users love the app, and we've just moved into a beautiful new office in Kuningan. It's a really exciting time for us.
options: The startup is already very profitable.
He didn't understand the question.
The startup probably isn't making a profit yet.
question.prompt: An investor asks Pak Hasan whether his startup is making a profit yet. Listen to his answer. What does it suggest?
question.explanation: He repeats the question (**A profit?**), so he understood it, and then talks about the team, the users and the office: everything except profit. If the startup were profitable, *yes* would be the easiest and best answer. Avoiding the point = probably not yet.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip each card. Say the English, or the real meaning, before you look.

flashcards.back: I'm not sure that's the best idea.
It might be worth looking at … again.

steps.title: Listen and read more
steps.text: A podcast episode on British indirectness (with a transcript), a short article on litotes, and one on sarcasm.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita melampaui kata-kata: membaca kode sopan yang dipakai orang di tempat kerja, menyampaikan sesuatu secara tidak langsung saat cocok, menangkap ironi dan understatement, dan memahami maksud sebuah jawaban dari apa yang dihindarinya. Putar setiap rekaman sesering yang kamu mau.

steps.title: Kode sopan
steps.text: Di C1 kamu sudah menangkap understatement, ironi, keengganan, penolakan halus dan pujian tipis dari kata-katanya. Sekarang lebih jauh: kode sopan yang dipakai orang di tempat kerja, terutama penutur British.
steps.body: Frasa-frasa halus ini membawa pesan yang lebih kuat. Yang paling penting: **I'm not sure that's the best idea** biasanya berarti **aku tidak setuju**, bukan benar-benar ragu. Cara membedakannya: orang yang ragu **meminta informasi** (*I'm not sure: when does testing finish?*); kode diikuti **alasan menolak** atau **usulan lain** (*Perhaps we could…*). Ini kecenderungan, bukan aturan: konteks yang menentukan.

steps.title: Dengarkan: jawaban untuk direktur
steps.text: Rapat pemasaran di Jakarta. Dengarkan frasa-frasa kodenya, lalu perhatikan apa yang mengikutinya.

question.listen: Spending the whole budget on one TV advert? I hear what you're saying, Pak Rudi, and it's certainly a brave plan. It might be worth looking at what happened with last year's campaign first. And perhaps keeping some money back for online ads.
options: She has no opinion yet and wants to hear more about the plan.
She thinks the plan is too risky and wants a smaller, safer one.
She admires the plan and wants to start soon.
question.prompt: Dalam rapat pemasaran, direkturnya, Pak Rudi, mengusulkan menghabiskan seluruh anggaran setahun untuk satu iklan TV. Dengarkan jawaban Sari. Sebenarnya apa maksudnya?
question.explanation: **I hear what you're saying** (= tapi aku tidak setuju) dan **a brave plan** (= berisiko) adalah kode sopan. Lalu ada hal yang perlu diperiksa dulu (**It might be worth looking at** kampanye tahun lalu) dan rencana yang lebih aman (**keeping some money back** untuk iklan online). Ia jelas punya pendapat: ia tidak bertanya apa-apa tentang rencananya, ia mengusulkan rencana yang lebih kecil.

steps.title: Menyampaikannya secara tidak langsung
steps.text: Sekarang sisi lainnya: memakai kode itu sendiri, dan tahu kapan tidak memakainya.
steps.body: Bicaralah tidak langsung saat hubungan itu penting: menolak, mengkritik ide atasan, memberi kode. Soal keselamatan, uang dan tenggat, bicaralah langsung. Tidak setuju dengan sopan = **lunakkan + alasan + alternatif**. British lebih banyak understatement (*not bad* = bagus; *quite good* sering = cuma lumayan); Amerika lebih langsung. Jembatannya: *iya* sering = aku dengar, *nanti dulu* = penolakan halus, *boleh juga* = setuju dengan hati-hati. **Jebakan:** dalam bahasa Inggris, *Yes* yang sopan terdengar seperti setuju.

steps.title: Giliranmu: tidak setuju dengan sopan
steps.text: Pilih jawaban yang sopan DAN jelas menunjukkan kamu tidak setuju.

options: Yes, of course, Bu Ani.
That's a terrible idea, Bu Ani. It won't work.
I'm not sure that's the best idea, Bu Ani: testing won't finish until the 20th. Could we keep the original date?
question.prompt: Manajermu, Bu Ani, ingin memajukan peluncuran produk dua minggu. Menurutmu itu ide buruk karena pengujian belum selesai. Dalam rapat dengannya dan tim, jawaban mana yang jelas tidak setuju tapi tetap sopan?
question.explanation: Lunakkan (**I'm not sure that's the best idea**) + alasan (pengujian baru selesai tanggal 20) + alternatif (tetap pakai tanggal semula). **Yes, of course** sopan, tapi ia akan mendengarnya sebagai setuju: jebakan *iya*. **That's a terrible idea** jelas, tapi terlalu blak-blakan untuk manajermu di depan tim.

steps.title: Ironi dan understatement: petunjuk dari kata
steps.text: Ironi British sering diucapkan dengan suara datar, dan audio kita juga satu suara yang tenang. Jadi kata-katanya adalah buktimu.
steps.body: **Ironi:** kata positif + situasi yang jelas buruk, frasa tetap (*Oh great*, *Well, that went well*) atau pujian berlebihan = kebalikannya. **Sarkasme** adalah ironi untuk mengejek orang: hati-hati. **Understatement:** jauh lebih sedikit dari kenyataan (*not exactly cheap* = mahal sekali). **Litotes:** *not* + kata lawannya (*not bad* = bagus, *hardly ideal* = buruk). **Humor kering:** *I've had worse days* setelah bencana = aku tetap tegar. Bandingkan kata dengan fakta; percayai faktanya.

Tidak murah juga sih. → mahal sekali

steps.title: Dengarkan: terjebak di bandara
steps.text: Dimas menelepon temannya dari bandara di Surabaya. Bandingkan kata-katanya dengan fakta yang ia sebut.

question.listen: Well, this is fun. The flight's been delayed three times, the only café is closed, and my phone's on two per cent. Honestly, I couldn't have planned a better start to my holiday.
options: He's enjoying it.
He's annoyed, and he's joking about it.
He's worried about missing work.
question.prompt: Dengarkan Dimas. Sebenarnya bagaimana perasaannya tentang awal liburannya?
question.explanation: Ironi: **this is fun** dan **I couldn't have planned a better start** berdampingan dengan tiga fakta buruk (tiga kali tertunda, kafe tutup, baterai hampir habis). Faktanya yang menang: ia kesal dan menjadikannya candaan. Tidak ada satu kata pun tentang pekerjaan.

steps.title: Giliranmu: litotes
steps.text: Dua understatement dalam satu kalimat. Apa cerita sebenarnya?

options: The panel were rather unfriendly, and her answer about salary went badly.
The panel were very friendly, and her answer about salary was perfect.
The panel were friendly, but her answer about salary was a little short.
question.prompt: Setelah wawancara kerja di Jakarta, teman Rina bertanya bagaimana hasilnya. Rina berkata: 'The panel weren't the friendliest people I've ever met, and my answer about salary was hardly ideal.' Apa maksudnya?
question.explanation: Litotes: **weren't the friendliest** = kurang ramah, dan **hardly ideal** = buruk. Keduanya melunakkan pesan negatif. Pilihan kedua membalik maknanya; pilihan ketiga mengarang detail (jawaban yang pendek) dan tidak menangkap bahwa *hardly ideal* berarti hasilnya buruk.

steps.title: Subteks: apa yang dihindari jawabannya
steps.text: Keterampilan terakhir: menangkap pesan dari apa yang tidak dikatakan sebuah jawaban.
steps.body: Filsuf Paul Grice menjelaskan **gagasan bahwa** orang yang bercakap-cakap saling bekerja sama: memberi informasi secukupnya, mengatakan yang benar, tetap pada topik dan jelas. Kalau sebuah jawaban jelas-jelas tidak begitu, ada pesannya. Perhatikan: **menghindari pokoknya**, **mengganti topik**, **alasan sebagai ganti jawaban**, **kata yang lebih lemah** (*most*, *some*) dan **tidak ada 'ya' untuk pertanyaan ya/tidak**. Kalau jawabannya memang ya, mudah sekali bilang ya.

steps.title: Dengarkan: pertanyaan soal laba
steps.text: Acara networking di Jakarta. Seorang investor mengajukan pertanyaan langsung kepada Pak Hasan.

question.listen: A profit? Well, we've got a fantastic team, our users love the app, and we've just moved into a beautiful new office in Kuningan. It's a really exciting time for us.
